cases.difference: DuckDB's ~ is a full match (regexp_full_match, false here); PostgreSQL's ~ is a partial match (true).
cases.sql: SELECT 'abc' ~ 'b' AS m;

cases.difference: DuckDB's !~ negates a full match (true here); PostgreSQL's negates a partial match (false).
cases.sql: SELECT 'abc' !~ 'b' AS m;
SELECT id, regexp_full_match(s, 'a.*') AS a, regexp_full_match(s, 'b|abc') AS b FROM r ORDER BY id;

SELECT id, s SIMILAR TO '(a|x)[a-z]*' AS a, s NOT SIMILAR TO '[a-c]+' AS b FROM r WHERE id <> 6 ORDER BY id;

cases.difference: PostgreSQL's SIMILAR TO uses SQL wildcards (% matches any text: true); DuckDB's SIMILAR TO is a regular expression where % is a literal (false).
cases.sql: SELECT 'abc' SIMILAR TO 'a%' AS m;

cases.difference: In PostgreSQL's SIMILAR TO . is a literal (false here); DuckDB treats it as any character (true).
cases.sql: SELECT 'abc' SIMILAR TO 'a.c' AS m;

cases.difference: DuckDB does not implement a custom SIMILAR TO escape (error); PostgreSQL answers false.
cases.sql: SELECT 'abc' SIMILAR TO 'a' ESCAPE '#' AS m;
cases.reference_error: Not implemented Error: Custom escape in SIMILAR TO

cases.difference: DuckDB (RE2) takes the first alternative that matches ('a': Xbcd); PostgreSQL takes the longest match ('ab': Xcd).
cases.sql: SELECT regexp_replace('abcd', 'a|ab', 'X') AS m;
SELECT regexp_replace('abcd', 'ab|a', 'X') AS a, regexp_replace('xaaay', 'a+', '-') AS b, regexp_replace('abab', 'ab', '', 'g') AS c;

cases.assay_error: unsupported: global regular expression replacement of an empty match
cases.difference: After replacing 'b', DuckDB skips the empty match that follows (-a-c-); PostgreSQL replaces it (-a--c-).
cases.sql: SELECT regexp_replace('abc', 'b*', '-', 'g') AS m;
SELECT regexp_replace('abc', 'b*', '', 'g') AS a, regexp_replace('abc', 'x*', '-', 'g') AS b, regexp_replace('abc', '', '-', 'g') AS c, regexp_replace('', 'x*', '-') AS d;

cases.difference: \0 is the whole match in DuckDB (a[b]c) and a literal \0 in PostgreSQL (a[\0]c).
cases.sql: SELECT regexp_replace('abc', 'b', '[\0]') AS m;

cases.difference: \& is the whole match in PostgreSQL (a[b]c); DuckDB rejects the rewrite and returns the text unchanged (abc).
cases.sql: SELECT regexp_replace('abc', 'b', '[\&]') AS m;

cases.assay_error: unsupported: replacement refers to a group
cases.difference: DuckDB returns the text unchanged (abc); PostgreSQL inserts an empty string (a[]c).
cases.sql: SELECT regexp_replace('abc', '(b)', '[\2]') AS m;

cases.difference: DuckDB's submatches follow the first matching alternative ([a|bc]); PostgreSQL's prefer the longest earlier group ([ab|c]).
cases.sql: SELECT regexp_replace('abc', '(a|ab)(bc|c)', '[\1|\2]') AS m;

cases.difference: For a repeated group DuckDB reports one long iteration (<ab|ab>cab); PostgreSQL splits it into more iterations (<ab|b>cab).
cases.sql: SELECT regexp_replace('abcab', '([ab]+)+', '<\1>') AS m;

cases.difference: PostgreSQL makes the whole match non-greedy when the first quantifier is lazy (x[a|]aay); DuckDB applies laziness per quantifier (x[a|aa]y).
cases.sql: SELECT regexp_replace('xaaay', '(a+?)(a*)', '[\1|\2]') AS m;

cases.sql: SELECT regexp_replace(s, '^b', '-', 'n') AS m FROM r WHERE id = 2;

cases.difference: DuckDB folds the Kelvin sign to k (true); PostgreSQL does not (false).
cases.sql: SELECT 'K' ~* 'k' AS m;

cases.assay_error: unsupported: case-insensitive regular expression on non-ASCII text
cases.difference: Case folding outside ASCII depends on each engine's Unicode tables; Assay refuses it in every function. DuckDB folds the long s to s (true).
cases.sql: SELECT regexp_matches('ſ', 'S', 'i') AS m;

cases.assay_error: unsupported: case-insensitive regular expression with non-ASCII
cases.difference: A non-ASCII letter in a case-insensitive pattern depends on Unicode case tables. DuckDB answers true.
cases.sql: SELECT regexp_matches('É', 'é', 'i') AS m;

cases.difference: \b is a word boundary in DuckDB (true) and a backspace in PostgreSQL (false).
cases.sql: SELECT regexp_like('a b', 'a\b') AS m;

cases.sql: SELECT regexp_like('ab', 'a(?=b)') AS m;
